alt.en: A printed book page numbered 28, headed "A Collection of" and "Carol IX." It has four numbered verses of words with no music, the first beginning "The first Nowel that the Angel did say", followed by a chorus, "Nowel, Nowel, Nowel, Nowel, Born is the King of Israel."
alt.es: Página impresa de un libro con el número 28 y los encabezados "A Collection of" y "Carol IX." Tiene cuatro estrofas numeradas de letra sin música, la primera empieza "The first Nowel that the Angel did say", seguida de un estribillo, "Nowel, Nowel, Nowel, Nowel, Born is the King of Israel."

caption.en: Carol IX on page 28 of Davies Gilbert's Some Ancient Christmas Carols, second edition (London, 1823): the earliest known printing of the words, with no tune, and already "certain poor Shepherds".
caption.es: El villancico IX en la página 28 de Some Ancient Christmas Carols de Davies Gilbert, segunda edición (Londres, 1823): la primera impresión conocida de la letra, sin melodía, y ya con "certain poor Shepherds".

source: Davies Gilbert (collector), Some Ancient Christmas Carols, with the Tunes to which they were formerly sung in the West of England, The Second Edition (London: printed by John Nichols and Son, 1823), Carol IX, p. 28
library: The Pennsylvania State University Libraries (digitized by Google; PDF at the Hymnology Archive)
callNumber: Google Books scan of the Penn State copy (Google ID not found); Hymnology Archive PDF Gilbert-SomeAncientChristmasCarols-1823-2ndEd.pdf, PDF p. 69
licenceEvidence: Title page: "The Second Edition. London: Printed by John Nichols and Son ... 1823." Davies Gilbert died 1839; the carol is traditional. Faithful scan of a flat page; the Google mark is cropped off (see rights.md).
credit: The Pennsylvania State University Libraries, digitized by Google

alt.en: A printed page of music headed "The First Nowell." in outlined capitals. The tune, in 3/8 with two sharps, is on the upper staff of each pair with the words in italic script under it, from "The first Nowell that the Angel did say" to "Born is the King of Israel", and a bass line on the lower staff.
alt.es: Página impresa de música con el encabezado "The First Nowell." en mayúsculas perfiladas. La melodía, en 3/8 y con dos sostenidos, va en el pentagrama superior de cada par con la letra en cursiva debajo, desde "The first Nowell that the Angel did say" hasta "Born is the King of Israel", y una línea de bajo en el pentagrama inferior.

caption.en: The First Nowell among the tunes at the back of William Sandys's Christmas Carols, Ancient and Modern (London, 1833): the earliest known printing of the tune, in D major and 3/8 with a bass line, with "certain poor Shepherds" under the notes.
caption.es: The First Nowell entre las melodías del final de Christmas Carols, Ancient and Modern de William Sandys (Londres, 1833): la primera impresión conocida de la melodía, en Re mayor y en 3/8 con una línea de bajo, con "certain poor Shepherds" bajo las notas.

source: William Sandys, Christmas Carols, Ancient and Modern (London: Richard Beckley, 1833), the airs at the back of the book (music, unpaginated), "The First Nowell"
library: University of California Libraries (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: Internet Archive christmascarolsa00sandrich, image n342; nrlf_ucb:GLAD-17147400
licenceEvidence: Published London 1833; William Sandys 1792-1874 (Internet Archive record, possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT). Faithful scan of a flat page, cropped to the carol (see rights.md).
credit: University of California Libraries, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A printed page of music headed "VI." and "The First Nowell." in italics, with four-part harmony on pairs of staves in 3/4 with two sharps, the words of the first verse under the upper staff, a section marked "Chorus" on "Nowell, Nowell, Nowell", and the page number 12 at the foot.
alt.es: Página impresa de música con el encabezado "VI." y "The First Nowell." en cursiva, con armonía a cuatro voces en pares de pentagramas en 3/4 y con dos sostenidos, la letra de la primera estrofa bajo el pentagrama superior, una sección marcada "Chorus" en "Nowell, Nowell, Nowell" y el número de página 12 al pie.

caption.en: No. VI in Bramley and Stainer's Christmas Carols New and Old (London, first published 1867; this printing of the 1870s): John Stainer's four parts in D major, the harmony most choirs still sing and the setting our arrangement is read from.
caption.es: El n.º VI de Christmas Carols New and Old de Bramley y Stainer (Londres, publicado por primera vez en 1867; esta impresión es de la década de 1870): las cuatro voces de John Stainer en Re mayor, la armonía que todavía cantan la mayoría de los coros y de la que parte nuestro arreglo.

source: H. R. Bramley and John Stainer, Christmas Carols New and Old, first series (London: Novello, Ewer and Co., undated, [187?]), No. VI, p. 12, "The First Nowell"

alt.en: A colour print of a photograph looking over the slate roofs and chimneys of stone houses to a harbour full of fishing boats, with a long pier, a curving bay, and a town and low green hills beyond.
alt.es: Impresión en color de una fotografía que mira, por encima de los tejados de pizarra y las chimeneas de unas casas de piedra, hacia un puerto lleno de barcos de pesca, con un muelle largo, una bahía curva y, más allá, un pueblo y colinas verdes y bajas.

caption.en: Newlyn, a fishing town in the far west of Cornwall, in the 1890s: in 1833 William Sandys wrote that in the West of England, "especially in the western parts of Cornwall", carol singers still went "from house to house".
caption.es: Newlyn, un pueblo pesquero del extremo oeste de Cornualles, en la década de 1890: en 1833 William Sandys escribió que en el oeste de Inglaterra, "sobre todo en las partes occidentales de Cornualles", los cantores de villancicos todavía iban "de casa en casa".

source: [Newlyn, general view, Cornwall, England], photochrom print no. 10748, Views of the British Isles (Detroit Publishing Co. catalogue, 1905)
